chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Alaa, from Muhammad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Muhrim (one in Ihram), if he dies, what is done with him? He said: 'Cover his face and do with him as is done with the non-Muhrim, except that perfume is not brought close to him.' And if the Muhrim wears a shirt intentionally, upon him is the blood-money of a sheep. And if he wears many garments, upon him is the ransom for each one of them.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What are the burial rites and financial penalties for a pilgrim in Ihram who dies or wears prohibited clothing?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the burial rites for a pilgrim in Ihram, emphasizing that death nullifies the state of Ihram, thus allowing the body to be treated as a regular deceased person except for the exclusion of perfume. It further details the financial expiation (dam) for intentional violations of clothing restrictions, distinguishing between the penalty for a single shirt and the cumulative liability for multiple garments, reflecting the juristic principle of proportional compensation for distinct transgressions.
